bug_semantics: FileBinding.write and ZipFileBinding.write derived a supposedly safe basename with controller-local java.io.File.getName(), then passed that string to hudson.FilePath for resolution on the node. A separator not recognized by the controller OS, notably backslash on a Unix controller, survived basename extraction and could be interpreted as traversal on a Windows node; attacker-controlled file or zip credential names could therefore escape the temporary secrets directory and write or unzip at arbitrary node paths, with possible code execution when a low-privileged job configurator can supply credentials to a job on the built-in node.
flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed (SECURITY-3672) first wrote the specific incomplete-sanitization mechanism in both binding classes: new File(credentials.getFileName()).getName() followed by dir.child(baseName). Its parent used the raw credential filename and did not contain this cross-filesystem basename mechanism; the attempted forward-slash traversal fix therefore left a separator-semantics bypass that SECURITY-3790 later corrected.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object author and committer are both Kevin-CB <kguerroudj@cloudbees.com>; the complete message is SECURITY-3672 and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: Vendor advisory https://www.jenkins.io/security/advisory/2026-05-27/#SECURITY-3790 states that Credentials Binding Plugin 720.v3f6decef43ea_ and earlier improperly sanitizes file and zip credential names, permits arbitrary node-filesystem writes, and is fixed in 725.ve52b_2328a_fde.

CVE.org record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-48922 was checked directly: cveMetadata.state is PUBLISHED, Jenkins is the CNA, and the affected boundary is <=720.v3f6decef43ea_; this is not withdrawn or rejected.

git -S on both src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/credentialsbinding/impl/FileBinding.java and ZipFileBinding.java identifies 3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed as the first writer of String baseName = new File(credentials.getFileName()).getName(); and e52b2328afdebcb69852687392fde94b174eaec4 as its remover.

git diff 80e905ef14eb17d43c454b65f1f9d4b9008c6743..3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed proves parent absence and BIC introduction in both bindings: the parent has dir.child(credentials.getFileName()), while the BIC adds java.io.File.getName() and then dir.child(baseName).

The BIC's SECURITY-3672 tests cover ../../../../ payloads, while direct fix e52b2328afdebcb69852687392fde94b174eaec4 adds SECURITY-3790 backslash traversal payloads plus dot, dot-dot, empty, slash, and backslash degenerate filename cases, matching the residual separator-sanitization flaw.

git diff 2965546b586225567b52cfc9b170b9f448729d32..e52b2328afdebcb69852687392fde94b174eaec4 shows the direct production fix in both binding classes: replace new File(...).getName() with new FilePath(new File(...)).getName().

Tag refs and ancestry checks show 720.v3f6decef43ea_ resolves exactly to BIC 3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed, 725.ve52b_2328a_fde resolves exactly to fix e52b2328afdebcb69852687392fde94b174eaec4, and the BIC is an ancestor of the fix.
git rev-list --parents -n 1 shows BIC 3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed has exactly one parent, 80e905ef14eb17d43c454b65f1f9d4b9008c6743; there is no merge or squash aggregate to decompose.
git cat-file -p and git log -1 on the BIC show Kevin-CB <kguerroudj@cloudbees.com> as both author and committer, a signed commit, and only the message SECURITY-3672 with no AI/coauthor trailer.
reasoning: The live Jenkins/CVE records confirm a real, published path-traversal vulnerability and the affected/fixed release boundary. Although the parent already passed the raw credential filename and was broadly unsafe, 3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed is the atomic first write of the specific residual mechanism audited here: a SECURITY-3672 sanitization attempt using controller-local java.io.File basename semantics before node-side FilePath resolution. Direct parent-tree diff proves that mechanism absent in 80e905ef14eb17d43c454b65f1f9d4b9008c6743. The forward-slash-only regression tests added by the BIC and the backslash/degenerate-name tests added by e52b2328afdebcb69852687392fde94b174eaec4 explain the bypass and its closure. Exact tag resolution places the BIC at affected release 720 and the direct fix at patched release 725. The one-parent BIC has no reconstructable squash members, and its commit object has human author/committer identity with no AI marker; therefore the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
